neighbours.label: the word right after a question noun or 'asked' that says who asks or what about (questions from, queries from, asked about, question about), as opposed to the same prepositions after letters, calls or money
fire: After the lecture the speaker answered questions from the students in the hall.
The clerk spends her day handling queries from worried tenants.
At the hearing the senator had a question about the missing funds.
Our guide patiently took questions from the tourists on the bus.
The new manager has been asked about the layoffs several times.
Parents wrote in with questions about the new bus schedule.
The help desk received dozens of queries from students last term.
Every journalist there had a question about the mayor's trip.
quiet: After the lecture the speaker collected essays from the students in the hall.
The clerk spends her day handling rent from worried tenants.
At the hearing the senator had a folder about the missing funds.
Our guide patiently took photos from the tourists on the bus.
The new manager has been warned about the layoffs several times.
Parents wrote in with complaints to the new bus company.
The help desk received dozens of parcels from students last term.
Every journalist there had a story about the mayor's trip.

short: word right after question, query or asked
notes: Card: ' from' x6, ' about', ' asked' after questions; the + pole has 'question of', 'question becomes'. Probes: questions from 0.76-1.11, question about 0.47, asks you about 0.85, asked about 0.24, questions on 0.20; letters from 0.16, money from 0.01, told about 0.07. 'inquiries about' reached only 0.05, so the noun set is narrow.
